subject: GreenfieldTech — Detailed IAM questionnaire and evidence

Subject: GreenfieldTech — Detailed IAM questionnaire

Monica,

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. GreenfieldTech is collecting detailed capability evidence as part of our RFP. Attached is our canonical IAM questionnaire (short version) — we need more detailed confirmation on the following for your hosted offering (production API + Redwood Console):

- SAML 2.0 support: SP-initiated vs IdP-initiated, metadata format, cert rollover process, single logout (SLO) support.
- OIDC: supported flows (auth code, client credentials), support for multiple redirect URIs per client, and refresh token lifetime.
- SCIM 2.0: full vs delta sync, supported resource types (User, Group), group membership provisioning, custom attribute mapping, rate limits and recommended throttling behavior.
- RBAC & Admin Controls: default roles, capability to create custom roles, tenant-level vs org-level admin separation, self-service admin UI.
- Audit & Logging: event types captured (auth, provisioning, role changes), retention window, export mechanisms (SIEM integrations, S3, or API).
- Evidence: config screenshots, SSO metadata XML, and any runbooks describing onboarding and certificate rollover.

Please send the answers inline where possible and attach any supporting artifacts. We have a technical review call scheduled the week of May 4–8; ideally we get documents ahead of that.

Thanks,
Emily Roy
Security Procurement
Greenfield Technologies

Subject: Re: GreenfieldTech — Detailed IAM questionnaire

Emily — thanks for the clear list. Attached is our consolidated response packet (PDF) and SAML metadata. Quick summary inline below; full answers and artifacts are in the attached PDF and the Drive link.

SAML 2.0:
- Support: Yes. Redwood supports both SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows.
- Metadata: We provide standard SAML 2.0 metadata XML; you can upload either the metadata file or the IdP metadata URL in the Console.
- Cert rollover: We support dual-certificate metadata (current + next) to enable seamless rollover. Our recommended process: upload replacement cert into Console, test with a non-production tenant, then finalize rollover. We document the steps in the attached runbook.
- SLO: Not supported across all flows today. We recommend configuring short session lifetimes and relying on our session invalidation API for explicit sign-outs. Roadmap item for SLO in H2 2026.

OIDC:
- Flows: Authorization code (PKCE), Client Credentials, and Device Code for unattended devices.
- Redirect URIs: Multiple redirect URIs per client allowed; granular audience and scope mapping supported.
- Refresh token policy: Configurable per client; default refresh token lifetime is 30 days for long-lived clients and 24 hours for SPA flows.

SCIM 2.0:
- Support: Yes, SCIM 2.0 core User and Group resources.
- Operations: Create/Replace/Delete and incremental (delta) changes are supported using standard list/since semantics.
- Custom attributes: Supported via a schema extension mechanism; mapping done in the Console during provisioning setup.
- Rate limits: Typical production tenant rate limit is 300 req/min for SCIM endpoints; we recommend exponential backoff.
- Deprovisioning latency: Typical near-real-time (<60s) for single-item changes; bulk provisioning may take minutes — details in PDF.

RBAC & Admin Controls:
- Default roles: org_owner, org_admin, tenant_admin, developer, billing_admin, read_only.
- Custom roles: Yes, via the Console and API; role permissions are granular (route/model/deployment level scoping supported).
- Separation: Org-level and tenant-level admin separation supported; cross-tenant actions restricted to org_owner role.
- Self-service UI: Admin Console provides role management, user invites, and permission previews.

Audit & Logging:
- Events captured: Auth successes/failures, token issuance, SCIM provisioning events, role/permission changes, API key rotations, and model deployment changes.
- Retention: Default 90 days in Console; extended retention (1 year+) available as an add-on with S3 export or SIEM push.
- Exports: Audit export API, direct S3 export to customer bucket, and webhook delivery to SIEM.

Next steps: attached PDF (Redwood_IAM_RFI_GreenfieldTech_20260503.pdf) contains config screenshots, the runbook for cert rollover, and end-to-end provisioning examples. Also attaching redwood-sso-metadata.xml for immediate import/testing. We propose a technical deep dive on Thu, May 7 at 10:00 PT (I'll follow up with a calendar invite).

Best,
Monica Patel
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Emily / Monica — quick clarification on SCIM rate limits and bulk behavior (adding here so it's in-thread and in the PDF errata):

- Rate limits: 300 req/min is per-tenant for our standard Dedicated/Hosted tiers. For enterprise customers in Redwood Dedicated we can configure higher per-tenant throughput; please flag if you anticipate >10k users/day provisioning spikes.
- Bulk provisioning: We support a SCIM bulk endpoint for batched imports; large imports are processed asynchronously — typical completion within 2–10 minutes depending on batch size.

Also noting that our SCIM implementation returns granular error payloads (bulk error indices) so you can identify specific failures without re-sending entire batches.

Aisha Rahman
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
